notes: Fictional entity in TBox: a made-up class of plays (newly found on papyrus) under a real class (complete ancient Greek tragedy). Determinate: two new plays named in the prompt (not by Euripides; complete). The two questions about the three surviving tragedians are determinate since 2026-10-31 (no, and yes): they had a world (w1) that kept the closed set 'every surviving complete tragedy is by one of the three' while holding the Ilvessan plays, which is not consistent (formal check, FINDINGS A1). With no indeterminate query left, the record has no worlds. Could it exist unrecorded: yes, as Menander's Dyskolos did. R1: Rhesus and Prometheus Bound have disputed authorship, but the standard statement is "only three authors". Replaces an earlier draft (a fourth Greek architectural order) that the record would certainly know of. Verifier: the edit now states that Ilvessan plays exist (found on papyrus in 2025), which the closed-set queries need; those queries and the bridge are phrased by attribution, so the disputed authorship of Rhesus and Prometheus Bound (still attributed to Euripides and Aeschylus) does not change the real answer.
